about: Warnings shown under a received message that matches one of these patterns (docs/design/blocking-and-safe-mode.md 6.3 and 10g). Read by both clients. A warning never blocks a message and never reports anything; it only explains. Matching: a message matches an entry when it contains any phrase in `any`, compared case-insensitively on whole words (a phrase is a run of words; punctuation between words is ignored). `applies_to` says whose messages it is shown on: `strangers` (anyone who has not given you a friendship pass) and `friends` (a friend's account can be taken over, so the money and phrase warnings apply to friends too). Add a pattern by adding a phrase or an entry; no code change is needed.

warnings.title: Asking for money
warnings.explain: Scams almost always end in a request for money: gift cards, wire transfers, crypto, or an investment that cannot lose.
warnings.advice: Do not send money or gift card codes to someone you have not met in person. If a friend asks, check with them another way first.

warnings.title: Asking for your recovery phrase or keys
warnings.explain: Your recovery phrase is your identity. Anyone who has it owns your account and everything in it.
warnings.advice: Nobody from HumanityOS or any server will ever ask for your recovery phrase. Never type it into a message.

warnings.title: Claiming to be staff
warnings.explain: Someone saying they are HumanityOS staff, support or a server admin may not be. A server's real roles show next to names in the member list.
warnings.advice: Check their role in the member list. Real admins never need your recovery phrase, passwords or money.

warnings.title: Moving the conversation somewhere else
warnings.explain: Asking to continue on another app, by phone or on a private video call moves you away from the tools here that protect you: Block, Report, and your safety settings.
warnings.advice: You can say no. Stay here until you know who they are.

warnings.title: Pressure or secrecy
warnings.explain: Pressure to act right now, threats about your account, or asking you to keep something secret are common ways to stop people from thinking twice or asking someone they trust.
warnings.advice: Take your time. It is always fine to talk to someone you trust before doing anything.
